deployNotes: Builder is a CLI/batch tool, not a long-running web service; deploy as a job-type pod that executes builds and exits.
The container mounts a volume at /data (or similar) for persistent artifact and metadata storage across invocations.
No database pod is required; metadata is stored as flat YAML/JSON files within the artifact directory.
The gui/ directory uses lorca (native Chrome webview) and is incompatible with headless container environments; only the CLI build pipeline is deployable on-cluster.
To build multi-language targets inside the container, install language toolchains (go, dotnet, javac, node, python3, ruby) in the image or mount them as sidecar volumes.

productionPlan.summary: Builder is a Go CLI that clones a repo, detects its language, compiles or packages it, and emits a zip artifact with build metadata. It runs to completion as a batch job with no web server or persistent daemon. The one thing that matters most is that the Dockerfile lacks a CMD to actually execute the built binary, so the job currently exits without doing any work.

decisions.decision: Single pod running as a Kubernetes job that executes a build and exits; no companion pods
decisions.why: Builder is a CLI tool invoked with `builder init [repo url]` or `builder` from a workspace — it performs a one-shot build and terminates, with no listening port or long-running process

decisions.decision: A 5 Gi volume mounted at /data for workspace, logs, artifact, and hidden directories that must survive restarts
decisions.why: The directory/ package creates hidden, logs, workspace, and artifact dirs on disk; without persistence the built artifacts and metadata are lost after the job pod is rescheduled

decisions.decision: Use golang:1.16-alpine matching go.mod's go 1.16 directive, add ENV GOTOOLCHAIN=auto, tini, ca-certificates, and a CMD that runs /go/src/builder/builder
decisions.why: The existing Dockerfile builds the binary but has no CMD or ENTRYPOINT so the container exits immediately without executing it; tini ensures proper signal handling and ca-certificates enables git clone over HTTPS

decisions.decision: Set resourceType to job (application.version 2.0) — Builder is a run-to-completion workload, not a deployment
decisions.why: Builder's main() dispatches a single command (init, config, or build) and returns; it never enters a loop or serves requests

decisions.decision: No servicePorts and no path — the job pod exposes no network endpoint
decisions.why: Builder only uses outbound git clone; it never listens on a port

fix_before_production.title: Add a CMD or ENTRYPOINT to execute the built binary
fix_before_production.why: The Dockerfile compiles /go/src/builder/builder but has no CMD — the container starts, does nothing, and exits immediately, so every job run completes with zero output

fix_before_production.title: Remove or gate the GUI mode (lorca) behind a build tag or runtime check
fix_before_production.why: main.go unconditionally imports the gui package which calls lorca (requires a native Chrome binary); running `builder gui` inside the container will panic at runtime

fix_before_production.title: Install language toolchains (dotnet-sdk, openjdk, node, python3, ruby) in the Docker image
fix_before_production.why: The compile/ package shells out to `dotnet publish`, `javac`, `npm`, `python`, `ruby` — without them every non-Go build silently fails inside the container

verify_after_deploy: `builder init https://github.com/example/go-hello` completes and produces a workspace directory with a builder.yaml and an artifact zip
The artifact directory contains both .json and .yaml metadata files alongside the zip
The job pod exits with exit code 0 and logs show 'Build Complete 🔨'
The volume at /data retains the artifact zip after the pod completes (check volume contents before reschedule)
open_questions: Which target languages must be buildable in production? This determines which toolchains to install in the image (Go only vs. all six supported languages).
Should this run as an on-demand Job (triggered externally) or a CronJob with a schedule (e.g., nightly rebuilds)?
Does the GUI mode need to remain in the binary at all, or can it be excluded from the production build via a separate entrypoint?
productionPlan.nexlayer_yaml:
application:
  name: builder
  version: 2.0
  pods:
    - name: builder
      image: "registry.nexlayer.io/YOUR_USER_ID/builder-builder:planned"
      resourceType: job
      command: "/go/src/builder/builder"
      vars:
        HOME: "/data"
      volumes:
        - name: artifacts
          mountPath: /data
          size: 5Gi

builds.notes: Rewrite the existing Dockerfile: keep golang:1.16-alpine as builder stage (matches go.mod), add ENV GOTOOLCHAIN=auto before go mod download, build with CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -ldflags="-w -s" -o /app/builder. Final stage: mirror.gcr.io/library/alpine:3.20, RUN apk add --no-cache ca-certificates tini git dotnet-sdk openjdk17 nodejs python3 ruby, COPY --from=builder /app/builder /usr/local/bin/builder, ENTRYPOINT ["/sbin/tini","--"], CMD ["builder"]. Ensure the binary binds to nothing (no port needed). Work in /data (volume mount) so artifacts persist.
